item.title: Quote of the day by The Notorious B.I.G: 'Stay far from timid, only make moves when your...'
item.description: Christopher Wallace, aka The Notorious B.I.G., imparted wisdom that resonates even after his passing. He emphasized the importance of pursuing authentic passions and being fearless in one's pursuit of dreams. Encouraging the belief that the sky's the limit, he highlighted ideals rooted in intrinsic motivation and bravery. His posthumous album embodies these lasting messages that continue to inspire generations.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by Tupac Shakur: 'Death is not the greatest loss in life. The greatest loss is...'
item.description: Experiencing the decline of one's inner spirit while still existing is a significant tragedy. This internal defeat surpasses physical death, which is a part of life. The profound insights of Norman Cousins and Tupac Shakur resonate here. Psychologists associate this phenomenon with learned helplessness. To avoid burnout, it is essential to make conscious, daily decisions that nurture and maintain one's inner energy.

item.title: Canada’s 2023 wildfires burned 15.1 million hectares and released 554 million tonnes of carbon
item.description: In 2023, Canada faced an unprecedented wildfire season that unleashed staggering carbon emissions from ancient underground soil and peat. These fires devastated extensive landscapes, liberating long-stored carbon accumulated over thousands of years. The challenge with subterranean fires lies in their resilience, transforming carbon sinks into sources of emissions, which exacerbates global warming and intensifies future wildfire risks.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Could D4vd face the death penalty? Los Angeles DA says D4vd is eligible for death penalty as prosecutors consider seeking execution in Celeste Rivas murder case
item.description: Singer D4vd, David Anthony Burke, faces potential death penalty charges. Prosecutors are weighing the death penalty for the murder of Celeste Rivas Hernandez. Burke has pleaded not guilty to all serious charges against him. The case moves forward after a judge found sufficient evidence for trial. His next court hearing is scheduled for August 31 in Los Angeles.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: Twitch streamer Ludwig makes surprise cameo in Road to Empress 2 as Prince of Fuling in Chinese live-action visual novel
item.description: Popular streamer Ludwig has surprised fans with an unexpected appearance in Road to Empress 2. He portrays the Prince of Fuling, an envoy with long blonde hair and blue royal attire. Players can unlock this special character after completing the game's main story. This collaboration highlights innovative ways game developers connect with online creators. Ludwig's unique role offers a fun bonus for both his fans and gamers.
item.dc:creator: Sumit Roy

item.title: A turtle left the ocean to lay eggs in Costa Rica with a remora attached; the fish held on for...
item.description: On a picturesque Costa Rican beach, an unexpected sight caught the eyes of researchers when a mother sea turtle arrived with a lively suckerfish clinging to her shell for an astonishing nineteen minutes. The fish, which seemed to adapt momentarily to land, showcased its gill movements. After careful observation, it was returned to its aquatic home, darting away with unexpected vigor, leaving onlookers astonished by its resilience.

item.title: Quote of the day by German philosopher Arthur Schopenhauer: "Great men are like eagles, and build their nest on…" - why distance from the crowd can shape extraordinary minds
item.description: Modern life demands constant connection and visibility, yet great thinkers need solitude. Arthur Schopenhauer believed eagles build nests in lofty solitude, mirroring deep thinkers. This chosen isolation fosters clear thought, creativity, and originality away from distractions. Solitude is distinct from loneliness, offering space for reflection and personal growth. Independent thinking and self-reliance are crucial for achieving true breakthroughs.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: $800 million Mega Millions jackpot won by Florida ticket holder after four-month wait
item.description: A lucky lottery player in Florida has finally claimed the massive $800 million Mega Millions jackpot after the prize went unclaimed for more than four months. According to the Mega Millions website, the winning ticket was sold in Florida for the Tuesday, July 28 drawing. The jackpot carried a cash option of $344.2 million and became the third Mega Millions jackpot to be won this year. It also ranks as the 10th-largest jackpot in the history of the lottery.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Africa’s richest billionaire plans to donate one-third of his wealth
item.description: Africa's richest man, Aliko Dangote, will donate one-third of his wealth to charity. This significant philanthropic commitment is part of his succession plan. His daughter, Halima Dangote, revealed this plan in a recent interview. The billionaire's fortune is valued at approximately $36.5 billion. This donation aims to embed philanthropy into the family's long-term vision.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Quote of the day by King Charles: "I'm a dangerous person because…" - a powerful lesson on caring deeply, speaking up and standing by your convictions
item.description: King Charles III's quote highlights the danger of caring deeply about issues. He acknowledged that his public activism as Prince of Wales would cease upon becoming king. Meaningful improvements often begin with individuals noticing potential for betterment. Strong convictions attract criticism, as history demonstrates with early environmental advocacy. Genuine engagement over passive observation drives progress and solves persistent problems.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Researchers mapped 5,600km of Canada’s coast using 170 years of records; kelp persistence reached...
item.description: Recent historic charts and satellite data illustrate the impressive durability of kelp forests on Vancouver Island. In cooler, wave-exposed zones, eighty-eight percent of kelp survived over a century, while warmer, sheltered waters faced a concerning decline to fifty-two percent. These insights reveal crucial regional variations in kelp forest resilience amid rising temperatures and serve as pivotal guidance for future conservation initiatives aimed at protecting these essential marine ecosystems.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: 500,000-year-old elephant bone tool found in England reveals advanced early human technology
item.description: An ancient elephant bone tool found in southern England reveals early human sophistication. This five-hundred-thousand-year-old implement was used for shaping stone tools precisely. Researchers found microscopic evidence of repeated use on the bone fragment. The discovery shows early humans planned and curated their technology carefully. This find offers new insights into Middle Pleistocene hominin intelligence and adaptability.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists discover ancient silk production in Uzbekistan nearly 2,000 years before the Silk Road
item.description: New evidence from Uzbekistan suggests ancient Central Asians raised silkworms around 2000 BCE. These findings challenge the traditional timeline for silk production in the region. Archaeologists discovered ancient silkworm cocoons and mulberry tree remains at Sapalli Tepe. This indicates local sericulture was established long before the Silk Road trade routes developed. These discoveries place silk production alongside other early Eurasian exchanges of knowledge and goods.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Teen donates handmade plushies to hospital
item.description: Sophie Histed, a thirteen-year-old, crocheted thirty plush toys for children. She learned the skill online and practiced for four years. These handmade toys were donated to the paediatric ward at Calvary North Adelaide Hospital. Hospital staff appreciated the thoughtful gesture and distributed the gifts. Sophie plans to continue her charitable crocheting efforts in the future.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: California researchers surveyed Point Reyes lagoon 19 times and found 73 pelicans killed by otters
item.description: Along California's Abbotts Lagoon, river otters have been spotted hunting brown pelicans, resulting in the discovery of seventy-three deceased pelicans during nineteen research visits. This unexpected predation correlates with the rising otter population in Northern California. While fish are their usual fare, larger birds provide a richer source of energy. Recent reports indicate that pelicans are adapting by learning to evade the hunting otters.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Scientists changed the fats in honeybees’ diets before pesticide exposure; survival rose to 90%, compared with below 50% on other diets
item.description: New research suggests honey bees can better survive pesticide exposure. Bees fed polyunsaturated fats showed a 90% survival rate. This dietary fat type also supported nerve function and energy balance. The findings indicate nutrition can strengthen bee resilience against agricultural stressors. This knowledge could inform bee diets and pollinator habitat planning.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk
